![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095196/assets/b2754f286de30f2017974030e571ec52f85bb84ad633912922a2b514728f3a7b.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=6,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=2,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-10,
$$

where ${C}_{1}$ is oriented clockwise and ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ are oriented counterclockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095196/assets/85a8ea287d2cb8e3b70e332ac444a9e06262fef35369d1bad1f24ea5c9d31687.png)

Notice that the positive orientations of the outer and inner curves are opposite those stated in the question.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & =-{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-6-2-(-10) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
